transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you too, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because my head just doesn't seem to stay on task anymore. Like, I'll be at work doing inventory, or... or trying to study for this supervisor certification, and I just keep reading the same line over and over. Or I'll walk into the supply closet and completely forget what I even went in there for. It's just getting really hard to focus on anything.
Have you struggled with this lack of focus your entire life, or is this something that has only started recently?

No, it hasn't been my whole life. It's been going on for about three years now. That's when the contractor I work for switched us over to rotating evening and overnight shifts at the larger properties we clean. It seems like it just started around then and hasn't let up.
Do you find yourself struggling to stay awake or feeling excessively sleepy during the day?

Yeah, I definitely do. My sleep has just been messed up for a long time now. It's like... after an overnight shift, I'll get home and just lie there in bed. I'm completely tired, but my brain feels wired, you know? And even on the days when I do actually manage to sleep a decent number of hours, I wake up feeling like I barely rested at all. So I'm pretty much always fighting off being sleepy.
Outside of the struggles with your sleep and focus, have you been feeling persistently sad, down, or have you lost interest in activities you used to enjoy?

Yeah, I have. Most days, it's like there's this heavy, flat feeling that just kind of follows me around. It doesn't really matter what I'm doing, either. Like, I could just be pushing my cleaning cart down an empty hallway at work, or even sitting at home with my family and trying to act normal... and that heavy feeling is just there. So yeah, I definitely feel down a lot of the time.
If you are able to take a few days off from work and return to a more typical daytime schedule, do your sleep problems and the heavy, down feeling improve?

Honestly, I'm not really sure. I haven't had the chance to take more than a day or two off in a row since this whole shift change started. We're pretty short-staffed, so getting a stretch of days off to actually try and reset my schedule just hasn't happened. So I couldn't tell you if going back to normal days would fix it or not.
Would you say that this heavy, flat feeling is present almost every day for most of the day, or are there times when you feel noticeably better or more energetic?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't exactly kept track of it. It feels like it's around a lot, but... I don't know if I could say for certain that it's every single day for most of the day. And as for feeling noticeably better or more energetic... I haven't really noticed any times like that lately. Between work and just trying to get through the week, it all just kind of blends together.
Looking back to when these problems first started three years ago, did the sleep issues begin before you started feeling that heavy, flat mood?

Thinking back three years... I really couldn't tell you which one came first. It's tough to remember the exact order of things. I just know they both started around that same time, but whether the sleep got bad before the heavy mood did, or if it was the other way around... I just don't know for sure. It all kind of blurred together back then.
When you are working your overnight shifts, what time do you typically try to fall asleep, and what time do you usually wake up?

I don't really have a set schedule for that, to be honest. Um... I just try to sleep whenever I can after I get off work. Sometimes I try to lay down right away, other times I'm just sitting around for a while first. I don't really pay attention to the clock, so I couldn't give you an exact time for when I fall asleep or when I wake up. It just kind of happens when it happens.
Since this started three years ago, have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or your weight?

No, not really. I mean, I haven't noticed any big changes. I just eat when I'm hungry, I guess. My clothes still fit about the same, so I don't think my weight has gone up or down much. It's just been pretty steady.
If something really good or exciting happens to you, does your mood lift, even if just for a little while?

Not really. I mean... I don't really have a lot of good or exciting things happen, but even if something okay happens, I don't feel much different. It's just... I just feel the same heavy way pretty much all the time. Nothing really shakes it off.
Over the past three years, have there been any periods lasting two months or longer where you felt like your mood was 'back to normal' and you weren't struggling with this heavy, flat feeling?

No, I haven't. Um... it's pretty much just been this way the whole time. I mean, maybe a day here or there isn't quite as bad, but definitely not two whole months of feeling normal. It just never really goes away.
